sentence_stem: Had the company invested in better security,
correct_completion: it would not have lost so much data last year.
full_sentence: Had the company invested in better security, it would not have lost so much data last year.
acceptable_variants: it probably wouldn't have lost so much data last year.
the losses would have been far smaller.

options.text: it would lose much data next year.
options.why_wrong: 'Would lose' with 'next year' describes a future result, but the stem is a past unreal condition about last year.

options.text: so it lost a lot of data last year.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals cause and effect, not a conditional result. The stem needs a hypothetical result clause.

options.text: it would not have lost so much data last year.
it will not lose data now.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' expresses a real future result, but an inverted 'had' sentence needs a hypothetical past result.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with inverted 'had' in place of 'if'
explanation: Inverted 'had' replaces 'if', so the stem is a third conditional describing a past situation that did not happen. The result clause must use 'would have' plus a past participle. Students often reach for a simple conditional or a simple past here, but English requires the perfect form in the result clause.
translation: Si la empresa hubiera invertido en mejor seguridad, no habría perdido tantos datos el año pasado.
